procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: Fatigue, weakness and bone pain despite osteoporosis treatment; CKD

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, weak, bones ache.

HPI: Since the fall (mentioned in November) the fatigue has not lifted. Now also generalized weakness - harder to carry laundry upstairs - and a deep ache in her shins, hips and low back, worse by evening. Has been on alendronate since May, taking it correctly. No fever, night sweats, cough change, or weight loss. Mood ok, sleeping fine. Breathing at her baseline.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Looks tired. Conjunctivae a little pale. Lungs distant, no wheeze. Heart regular. Mild bilateral ankle edema, trace. Diffuse mild tenderness over tibiae, no point tenderness of spine. Strength 5-/5 proximally, symmetric. No synovitis.

A/P:
1. Fatigue/weakness/bone pain on alendronate - CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, vitamin D, iron studies today. Given CKD 3b and osteoporosis, I want endocrinology to look at bone and mineral metabolism; referral placed.
2. Edema trace - likely amlodipine; observe.
3. T2DM - A1c today.
Will message results.

documents.title: Results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Beverly - your hemoglobin is low at 10.8 (it was 12 in 2019). The red cells are normal-sized and iron, B12 and thyroid are fine, so this looks like the anemia that comes with kidney disease. Creatinine is up a little to 1.6. Vitamin D is fine at 34. A1c 8.6, slightly better. I've sent the endocrinology referral; their office will call. Let me know if you feel worse in the meantime.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULT
Visit date: 02/18/2021
Referring: primary care

Reason for referral: persistent fatigue, generalized weakness and bone pain that has not improved on osteoporosis therapy.

History: 67-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes and hypertension of long standing, with steadily falling kidney function over many years, now CKD 3b and followed by nephrology. Osteoporosis diagnosed last spring (DXA lumbar spine T -2.8), on alendronate since May 2020. Reports months of tiredness, weakness and aching bones. RA and severe COPD on daily prednisone 10 mg and weekly methotrexate.

Medications (per patient list): metformin 1000 BID, glyburide 5, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 12.5, omeprazole 20, prednisone 10, methotrexate 15/wk, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol PRN, aspirin 81, alendronate 70/wk, calcium carbonate 600 TID, cholecalciferol 2000 IU.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother T2DM and osteoporosis; father HTN and COPD; maternal aunt hip fracture.
Social: never smoker, wine occasionally, retired administrative assistant.

Exam: Mild edema of both lower legs. Pallor. No thyroid enlargement. Proximal strength mildly reduced. Spine non-tender.

Data: Hemoglobin 10.8, normocytic (PCP labs 1/12). Today: creatinine 1.6, calcium 9.3, phosphorus 4.6, intact PTH 186 pg/mL. 25-OH vitamin D 34 in January. DXA 4/2020 reduced bone density as above.

Assessment:
1. Hyperparathyroidism with normal calcium and raised PTH in the setting of CKD 3b - secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin. I spoke with her nephrologist, who reads the labs the same way.
2. Normocytic anemia, iron replete - anemia of CKD; nephrology will follow.
3. Osteoporosis on alendronate; bone pain likely reflects mineral-bone disease of CKD in part.

Plan: No medication change. Continue vitamin D3 2000 IU and calcium. Nephrology to trend PTH and phosphorus. Return to endocrinology in one year.

Endocrinology clinic

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccine dose 2 (pharmacy)
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Dose 2 of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine given 2/27/21 at her pharmacy, pulled from registry. Primary series complete.

documents.title: Endocrinology letter reviewed with patient
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt per PCP to go over the endocrinology letter. Explained the parathyroid finding is related to her kidneys and that nephrology will follow the blood tests; no new medicines. She was relieved there is a reason for the tiredness. Continue calcium and D. Has nephrology f/u in October. No questions.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 04/19/2021  Discharged: 04/28/2021

Principal diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of COPD with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure.

Course: 67F with severe COPD (FEV1 41% predicted 2017), never smoker, on chronic prednisone 10 mg, presented by ambulance with two days of increasing dyspnea and wheeze. Tiring in the ED despite bilevel support and was intubated. ICU 4 days, extubated after 3 days on the ventilator. Treated with IV methylprednisolone, nebulized bronchodilators and a course of antibiotics. SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative. Chest film without pneumonia. Transferred to the floor, ambulating with PT by day 7, on room air at discharge.

Discharge medications: home regimen unchanged, including prednisone 10 mg daily (steroid course completed in house), fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol, metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, omeprazole, methotrexate weekly (held in house, resume next week), aspirin, alendronate, calcium, vitamin D3.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit, one week out from an admission with intubation for a COPD flare. RN called her 4/29 (2 business days). Discharge summary reviewed.

She is shaken by the ICU stay. Breathing now back close to usual; walks to the mailbox without stopping. No fever. Sputum back to clear. Methotrexate restarted last week per discharge.

Meds reconciled against discharge list - no changes.

Exam: Vitals as charted, SpO2 on room air as charted. Diminished breath sounds, scattered end-expiratory wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. Trace ankle edema, unchanged.

A/P: COPD exacerbation, resolved; severe COPD. Reviewed inhaler technique again. Action plan: call us the same day for increased sputum or dyspnea. Continue current regimen. BMP/CBC today after steroids. Follow up at wellness visit in July.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.

Interval: April admission for COPD with intubation; recovered. Endocrinology in February: secondary hyperparathyroidism and anemia from CKD, no drug changes. COVID series done.

Functional: independent; slower on stairs since spring. No falls. Husband well, they split chores. Vision/hearing ok. Health care proxy on file.
PHQ-2: 1 (some low days after the hospital).

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs distant, no wheeze today. Heart regular. Feet: monofilament intact, DP pulses present, skin intact.

Plan: labs today. Diabetes still above goal; she again prefers diet over a new agent, and is aware of my concern. Mammogram next due 2022. Flu and COVID booster in early fall. RTC after labs as needed, otherwise late fall.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Booster eligible (65+, immunosuppressed). Flu high-dose left arm, Pfizer booster right arm. Tolerated well, observed 15 minutes. Reminded her to call if fever over 101 lasts more than a day.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology follow-up 10/19/2021.

CKD 3b with secondary hyperparathyroidism and anemia of CKD. Creatinine around 1.6. Hemoglobin about 11, iron replete; no ESA indicated at this level. PTH trending in the 180s with normal calcium and phosphorus at the upper end of normal; continue vitamin D3 and dietary phosphorus advice (handout given). BP fine. Hospitalized in April for COPD; renal function held through it.

Plan: no medication changes. Labs every 6 months via PCP. Return 1 year.

Outside Nephrology Group

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - regional hospital
Admission 11/08/2021 - Discharge 11/18/2021

Diagnosis: COPD exacerbation with acute respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation (second this year).

Summary: 67-year-old woman, never smoker, severe COPD on ICS/LABA, chronic prednisone 10 mg for COPD and RA, admitted in April with intubation. Two days of worsening breathlessness and cough at home; arrived hypoxic and hypercapnic, failed noninvasive ventilation within hours, intubated in the ED. Ventilated 2 days. IV corticosteroids, scheduled nebulizers, empiric antibiotics. COVID PCR negative. CXR hyperinflation, no infiltrate. Extubated without difficulty, weaned to room air, physical therapy cleared her for home.

Discharge meds: no changes to her home list. Prednisone continues 10 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: PCP 1-2 weeks.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Second COPD admission this year, again intubated (2 days). Home since 11/18; husband with her today.

Now: dyspnea at baseline, no fever, cough minimal. Using controller twice daily, albuterol 1-2 times a day. Med list matches discharge. She asks whether this will keep happening; we talked honestly about how serious her lung disease is and what she can do early in a flare.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Prolonged expiration, faint wheeze at bases. Heart regular. No edema beyond trace.

A/P: COPD exacerbation resolved; severe COPD with two intubations in 2021. Continue current inhalers and prednisone. Written action plan updated. Vaccines current. Labs today (post-steroid glucose, MTX labs). RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Eye exam 11/30/2021, dilated. Acuity 20/25 OU corrected. Pressures normal. Early cataract, stable. No diabetic retinopathy. No macular edema. Next exam 1 year.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: RA follow-up, 12/14/2021. Two COPD admissions this year, MTX held briefly each time and resumed. Joints quiet; no synovitis. Monitoring labs reviewed from PCP, counts and LFTs acceptable, creatinine 1.6. Prednisone 10 mg daily continues (also for lungs). Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly. Return 12 months.
